Script.name: vidblain
Script.script:
--[[ Vidblain coordinates Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
Vidblain drops you somewhere random and the way out is a fixed coordinate: the Zenith Trail to Omen Tor is at 11,8, Fury City at 11,26, and so on. The MUD tells you where you are on every room, so put it where you'll see it.
Below the Basement Staircase {coords}0,30,20
The tag is 'zone,x,y', or a bare '{coords}-1' outside a coordinate area. It is always gagged - we took it off the tag gag's list so we could read it, so hiding it is now our job and has to happen whether or not we display it.
The reading goes in a small draggable panel of its own, with the position as the title: there is nothing else to put in a box that size.
The axes, measured rather than assumed - 24,18 then 'run 2s5e' lands on 29,20, so x grows EAST and y grows SOUTH. y running southward is the surprising half and the reason this wasn't left to a guess.
The learning is still here and still runs: if any of that is ever wrong, one clean move corrects it and the correction sticks. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.vid = aardkit.vid or {}
local VB = aardkit.vid local U = aardkit.util
local CFG = U.load("vidblain", { show = "coordareas", -- coordareas | always | off (when to fill the panel) marks = {}, -- name -> {x=,y=} target = nil, -- which compass direction each axis grows in; measured, and re-learned if a -- move ever disagrees axis = { xdir = "east", ydir = "south" }, })
VB.zone, VB.x, VB.y = nil, nil, nil
-- Consoleless: the title carries the reading, so there's nothing to put in a -- body. Small enough to tuck anywhere, and the panel manager remembers where. local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "coords", title = "Location: -", x = "10px", y = "620px", width = 210, height = 34, consoleless = true, })
VB.panel = panel
local function settitle(txt) local h = panel and panel.holder if h and h.setTitle then pcall(function() h:setTitle(txt, "#3ad07a", "cb12") end) end end
local last = { x = nil, y = nil, dir = nil }
-- Aardwolf's own names for the places worth reaching, straight off 'speedwalks' local KNOWN = { ["omen tor"] = { 11, 8 }, ["asherodan"] = { 10, 15 }, ["darklight"] = { 14, 23 }, ["imperial"] = { 23, 4 }, ["sendhia"] = { 5, 6 }, ["fury"] = { 11, 26 }, }
local function inzone() return VB.zone ~= nil and VB.x ~= nil end
local function vidblain() local z = gmcp and gmcp.room and gmcp.room.info and gmcp.room.info.zone return z == "vidblain" end
--- -- axis learning -- -- One clean move teaches it: if east changed x by +1 then +x is east. Diagonals -- and anything that moved both axes are ignored - they'd teach it nothing. ---
local function learn(dx, dy, dir) local a = CFG.axis or {} if (dir == "east" or dir == "west") and dx ~= 0 and dy == 0 then a.xdir = (dx > 0) == (dir == "east") and "east" or "west" elseif (dir == "north" or dir == "south") and dy ~= 0 and dx == 0 then a.ydir = (dy > 0) == (dir == "north") and "north" or "south" else return end CFG.axis = a U.save("vidblain", CFG) end
function VB.on_move(dir) last.dir = dir end
--- -- the tag ---
function VB.on_coords(zone, x, y) -- Gag first and unconditionally. This used to sit inside the display path, -- so anywhere the panel had nothing to say the raw tag printed instead. deleteLine() zone, x, y = tonumber(zone), tonumber(x), tonumber(y)
if last.x and x and last.dir then learn(x - last.x, y - last.y, last.dir) end last.x, last.y, last.dir = x, y, nil
VB.zone, VB.x, VB.y = zone, x, y VB.stamp() end
function VB.on_nocoords() deleteLine() VB.zone, VB.x, VB.y = nil, nil, nil last.x, last.y = nil, nil settitle("Location: -") end
-- how far, and which way, to the active target function VB.delta() local t = CFG.target if not (t and inzone()) then return nil end local dx, dy = t.x - VB.x, t.y - VB.y if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then return "here" end
local a = CFG.axis if not (a and a.xdir and a.ydir) then return string.format("%+d,%+d", dx, dy) -- honest until it has learned end local out = {} if dx ~= 0 then local way = (dx > 0) and a.xdir or (a.xdir == "east" and "west" or "east") out[#out + 1] = math.abs(dx) .. way:sub(1, 1) end if dy ~= 0 then local way = (dy > 0) and a.ydir or (a.ydir == "north" and "south" or "north") out[#out + 1] = math.abs(dy) .. way:sub(1, 1) end return table.concat(out, " ") end
-- the delta as something you can actually type function VB.runcmd() local t = CFG.target local a = CFG.axis if not (t and a and a.xdir and a.ydir and inzone()) then return nil end local dx, dy = t.x - VB.x, t.y - VB.y if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then return nil end
local parts = {} if dy ~= 0 then local way = (dy > 0) and a.ydir or (a.ydir == "south" and "north" or "south") parts[#parts + 1] = math.abs(dy) .. way:sub(1, 1) end if dx ~= 0 then local way = (dx > 0) and a.xdir or (a.xdir == "east" and "west" or "east") parts[#parts + 1] = math.abs(dx) .. way:sub(1, 1) end return "run " .. table.concat(parts) end
--- -- the panel ---
function VB.stamp() -- 'off' used to save and then do nothing at all: the panel kept updating and -- the only way to be rid of it was 'panel coords hide'. if CFG.show == "off" then panel:hide(); return end
if not inzone() then settitle("Location: -"); return end if CFG.show == "coordareas" and not vidblain() then settitle(string.format("Location: %d,%d", VB.x, VB.y)) return end
local d = VB.delta() if d and d ~= "here" then settitle(string.format("%d,%d → %s", VB.x, VB.y, d)) elseif d == "here" then settitle(string.format("%d,%d arrived", VB.x, VB.y)) else settitle(string.format("Location: %d,%d", VB.x, VB.y)) end end
--- -- commands ---
function VB.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest)
if verb == "" or verb == "status" then local rows = { { "here", inzone() and (VB.x .. "," .. VB.y .. " (zone " .. VB.zone .. ")") or "no coordinates here" }, { "target", CFG.target and (CFG.target.name .. " " .. CFG.target.x .. "," .. CFG.target.y) or "none" }, { "to go", VB.delta() or "-" }, { "axes", CFG.axis and ("+x " .. (CFG.axis.xdir or "?") .. ", +y " .. (CFG.axis.ydir or "?")) or "not learned yet - move once" }, { "run", VB.runcmd() or "-" }, { "show", CFG.show }, { "" }, } for k, v in pairs(KNOWN) do rows[#rows + 1] = { " " .. k, v[1] .. "," .. v[2] } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "vid <name|x,y>", "set the target and show the way" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "vid run", "send the run command for the straight line" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "vid clear", "drop the target" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "vid show off|coordareas|always", "when the panel has anything to say" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "vid panel [show|hide|dock|embed]", "move it or put it away" } U.help("Vidblain", rows)
elseif verb == "run" or verb == "go" then local c = VB.runcmd() if not c then U.warn("No target, or you're already on it. 'vid omen tor' first.") else -- Vidblain is a maze, so this walks the straight line and the MUD -- gives up after three blocked moves. Run it again from wherever -- you end up; it's a nudge, not a pathfinder. U.ok(c) send(c, false) end
elseif verb == "clear" then CFG.target = nil; U.save("vidblain", CFG); U.ok("Target cleared.")
-- 'vid panel <verb>' rather than 'vid dock' etc, because 'vid show' is already -- the display mode and the two were colliding - the panel one was reachable -- only as the undiscoverable 'vid show2'. elseif verb == "panel" then if rest == "" then rest = "toggle" end aardkit.panel.cmd("coords " .. rest)
elseif verb == "show" then if rest == "off" or rest == "always" or rest == "coordareas" then CFG.show = rest; U.save("vidblain", CFG) if rest ~= "off" then panel:show() end VB.stamp() U.ok("Coordinates: " .. rest .. ".") else U.warn("vid show off|coordareas|always") end
else local x, y = arg:match("^%s*(%-?%d+)%s*,%s*(%-?%d+)%s*$") if x then CFG.target = { name = x .. "," .. y, x = tonumber(x), y = tonumber(y) } else local k = arg:lower() for name, c in pairs(KNOWN) do if name:find(k, 1, true) then CFG.target = { name = name, x = c[1], y = c[2] } break end end end if not CFG.target or (x == nil and not CFG.target.name:find(arg:lower(), 1, true)) then U.warn("Don't know '" .. arg .. "'. Try 'vid' for the list, or 'vid 11,8'.") return end U.save("vidblain", CFG) U.ok("Target " .. CFG.target.name .. " at " .. CFG.target.x .. "," .. CFG.target.y .. (VB.delta() and (" - " .. VB.delta()) or "")) end end
-- Mudlet doesn't say which way you went, but it does say what you sent, and -- that's enough: one plain 'east' with a clean coordinate change teaches it. local DIRS = { n = "north", north = "north", s = "south", south = "south", e = "east", east = "east", w = "west", west = "west", }
U.killhandler(aardkit_vid_send) aardkit_vid_send = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysDataSendRequest", "aardkit.vid.on_send")
function VB.on_send(_, cmd) local d = DIRS[U.trim(tostring(cmd or "")):lower()] if d then VB.on_move(d) end end
aardkit.register("vid", "Vidblain coordinates and where you're heading", VB.cmd)
